methods: distance from a point to a line
statement: For the ellipse $\\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ with $a>b>0$, let the foci be $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$. Show that the product of the perpendicular distances from $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$ to any tangent to the ellipse equals $b^{2}$.
solution:
Write a tangent in gradient form $y=mx\\pm\\sqrt{a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}}$, i.e. $mx-y\\pm\\sqrt{a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}}=0$. The foci are at $(\\pm c,0)$ where $c^{2}=a^{2}-b^{2}$. The perpendicular distance from $(c,0)$ is $d_{2}=\\dfrac{|\\pm\\sqrt{a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}}-mc|}{\\sqrt{1+m^{2}}}$ and from $(-c,0)$ is $d_{1}=\\dfrac{|\\pm\\sqrt{a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}}+mc|}{\\sqrt{1+m^{2}}}$. Their product is $d_{1}d_{2}=\\dfrac{|(a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2})-m^{2}c^{2}|}{1+m^{2}}=\\dfrac{|a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}-m^{2}(a^{2}-b^{2})|}{1+m^{2}}=\\dfrac{|b^{2}+b^{2}m^{2}|}{1+m^{2}}=b^{2}$.
